quote:
Tree
species with dynamic canopy and performing hydraulic function
with deep root system were found to be suitable for both ﬂooding
and drought situations but for different reasons. Deeps roots do not
have access to the richer soil horizons and therefore tree canopy
will grow slower even in the presence of excess water (ﬂooding)
and the tree canopy will produce less shade. In drought situation,
deep roots are appropriate to perform water redistribution that
will beneﬁt the associated crops in making water and nutrients
available to them (Coulibaly et al., 2014).
values: For flooding, deep roots limit nutrient-driven canopy growth and shading; for drought, they redistribute water. No named taxon, threshold or weight is supplied.
